requirement:
The instructions supplied under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions` tell the agent to call `finish_search` for every delivered
page before submitting its answer. They explain how to select the tags of
excerpts used as evidence and how to pass `used: []` when none contributed.
Finishing a page records the selected inputs without fetching more source.

It must tell the agent to call `finish_search` for every delivered page before submitting. It must explain how to select the tags of excerpts used as evidence and how to pass `used: []` when none contributed. It must state that finishing a page records the selected inputs without fetching more source.

They could live in any module. The agent would see the same content in every case, so the clause would hold under all of them. The same applies to the other clauses.

Its rules about when the field appears govern delivery, not this content requirement. No implementation roots are supplied, and none are needed. It takes the `instructions` string from the first `search_text` result, which has no matches. It then asserts that the string contains each of these phrases:
- "Before submitting, close every delivered search page". This covers the instruction to finish every delivered page before submitting.
- "finish_search". This names the tool.
- "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read". This explains how to select tags.
- "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result". This explains the `used: []` case.
- "without reading more source". This says finishing fetches no more source.

The test also asserts that the structural search's first result carries identical instructions (`page["instructions"] == instructions`), so the content is the same for both search kinds. Its use of `finish_search` shows that the described behavior matches what the tool actually does: `used: []` returns no dependencies, and selecting a tag records a dependency on that excerpt's node.
